# PR #1815: Patch: the AI's search keeps a play's placements apart when they differ only in lane, so trying every lane is not undone

Closes #1797

## What changed

The beam's duplicate check used to merge two positions that differed only in which lane a unit stood in. So most of the placements the root tries (#1635) were dropped before the opponent's reply could price them. This change keeps them apart. It does not put the lane variants in the beam itself, because they would score the same there and crowd out other plays.

- **`crates/ai/src/simulate.rs`**: new `unit_lanes(state)` gives every active unit's lane. `search_signature` itself is unchanged, so the lethal solver's visited set reads positions exactly as before.
- **`crates/ai/src/search.rs`** (`beam_search_with`):
  - Duplicates are now dropped by `(search_signature, unit_lanes)`, so two orders of the same moves into the same lanes are still one position.
  - The first child of each `search_signature` is scored, ranked and expanded exactly as before, so the frontier and the nodes it spends do not change.
  - A later child that differs from it only in its units' lanes is a **lane variant**. At most `AI_SEARCH.zone_variants` − 1 (that is, 1) are kept per position. A variant is never expanded.
  - If the frontier kept its position's first child, the variant ends its turn after the loop, after the lines still open. It costs one node from the beam's slice and joins the complete lines, losing ties to the old line.
- **`crates/ai/src/decide.rs`** (`best_per_first_action`): a finalist that differs from a better one only in its lane, with exactly the same score, is dropped. Lanes the reply tells apart (the Cleaver) stay separate finalists.
- **`crates/server/tests/fixtures/practice-claim.json`**: re-recorded, because the AI now picks different lanes in that game.
- Docs: `crates/ai/README.md`, the `beam_search` doc, and the `zone_variants` doc in `config.rs` (now with the screen's numbers).

## Where I departed from the plan, and why

- **The plan's cap failed an existing test.** Its design (up to 2 lane variants per position, kept open in the beam) failed `even_trades::decide_trades_into_the_taunt_rather_than_cast_hit_job_on_a_hand_that_fills_the_root` (#1779). A trace showed why: the four lines kept at depth 1 became Hit Job followed by a Vanilla in lane 1 or lane 2, all scoring −6.8. That pushed out the trade line (−9.004), and the AI cast Hit Job instead of trading. That is the crowding the issue warned about, so I did not edit that test.
- **The plan's position key is not fully lane-blind.** Units sign in board order, so lanes to the left and right of an existing unit were already different positions. Only lanes on the same side were being merged.
- **The decide.rs change was not in the plan.** Without it, the existing `decide::tests::a_refused_choice_submits_the_runner_up_lines_first_action_not_end_turn` (#1575) failed. On an empty board the Menace's lane 2 became a finalist identical to lane 1 and took the Vanilla's runner-up place. I left that test unchanged; it passes.
- **Parent commit**: the base is `db8d97fad`, not the plan's `633568b99`. The commits in between touch only the web client and the patches log.

- **Each unit's lane, not its own-side neighbours, for the duplicate check.** It is simpler, and the backrow part of the signature already reads positions.
- **Lane variants are closed, not kept open in the frontier.** Rejected: the plan's cap, which failed #1779's test. Also rejected: letting variants fill only the frontier slots no other position wants, which never fires on the Cleaver board, because it already has four distinct root moves.
- **Variants are closed after the loop, and only beside a first child the frontier kept.** Rejected: closing every variant, which would add finished lines for positions the beam had already discarded.
- **`AI_SEARCH.zone_variants` is reused, with no new constant.** Deeper levels already cap a play's lanes at it.
- **The finalist merge uses exact score equality.** Lanes that are symmetric for the reply produce identical numbers. Rejected: editing the #1575 test to accept a lane variant as its runner-up.

- A lane variant that stops at the seat's own prompt is scored where it stands, as lines left open at max depth already are.
- Variant closes spend nodes from the beam's slice; when the slice is spent, a variant is scored without ending its turn.

# #1797: Patch: the AI's search keeps a play's placements apart when they differ only in lane, so trying every lane is not undone
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
When the practice AI considers playing a unit, it is meant to try every lane that would make a difference: next to a friendly unit, away from an enemy that hits neighbours, or opposite a particular card. But a duplicate check later in its search treats two boards as the same when the only difference is which lane a unit stands in. So it throws away every such lane but the leftmost before it can compare them. In practice, the AI only chooses lanes well when the lane changes something immediately. Otherwise it takes the first open spot, even when that spot is next to the unit an enemy with Cleave is about to hit. Once built, it keeps those placements and can choose between them.

## Why
- The search's root tries a play in every distinct placement (#1635; `crates/ai/README.md:72-73`, `config.rs:91-97`, `root_candidate_set` at `candidates.rs:557-561`). Placements are told apart by `placement_key` (`candidates.rs:75-97`), which reads the neighbours and the lane's four zones.
- The beam then drops an open child whose `search_signature` it has already seen (`search.rs:209-215`). That signature leaves a unit's lane out on purpose: "A unit's lane is left out, so the two lanes `candidate_actions` keeps for one play stay one position" (`simulate.rs:835-836`). The unit part (`simulate.rs:863-879`) has no slot.
- Units are signed in board order. With one friendly unit in lane 1, a new unit in lane 2, 3 or 5 signs the same `[old, new]` every time, and only lane 2 survives.
- So the every-placement root helps only cards whose lane changes the board at once, like Lane Eater and Mushroom Power in the #1635 tests.
- It doesn't help placements whose worth shows later, even though the evaluation can see them: the imagined enemy reply prices Cleave damage to neighbours (`reply.rs:96-107`, `AI_REPLY.cleave_share`).
- #1635's own screen read 197-203, an edge of -0.015 (`config.rs:96-97`). That fits most of its new placements never reaching the comparison.

## Proposal
- Give the beam's duplicate check a placement-aware signature: add each unit's lane, or its own-side neighbours, to the unit part. Use it for the beam's `seen` set only. The lethal solver's visited set (`lethal.rs:230`, `:244`) keeps today's signature, so its cost doesn't grow.
- Stop lane variants that score the same from filling the beam (`beam_width` 4). Either keep one open child per play and score, or cap a play's lane variants in the frontier at `AI_SEARCH.zone_variants`.
- Any new number is a named constant in `config.rs` (CLAUDE.md rule 9).

## Where it lands
- `crates/ai/src/simulate.rs` (the signature), `crates/ai/src/search.rs` (the beam's duplicate check)
- `crates/ai/tests/ai/search.rs` (`mod lanes_that_play_differently`), `crates/ai/README.md`
- §3.1 (lanes and adjacency), §6 Cleave, §9.9 (the AI)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Search test: an enemy Cleave attacker is on the board, one AI unit stands in lane 1, and a vanilla unit is in hand. `beam_search`'s lines include the vanilla placed in a lane not next to the friendly unit.
- [ ] `decide` test: in that position, when the enemy's reply would cleave the neighbour, the AI places the new unit away from it.
- [ ] Two orders of the same moves into the same lanes still count as one position (the existing search tests pass).
- [ ] The lethal solver's results on the existing puzzles don't change.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-ai`, clippy, fmt and `cargo jackioh gate` pass.
- [ ] An improve-dev screen of 400 games against the parent build is reported in the pull request.

## Size and risks
Medium. Risks:
- More distinct open lines per level can crowd out other plays at `beam_width` 4; the cap guards against this.
- Decisions may get slower. Watch R977000's timing and the perf gate.
- The static evaluation alone can't tell lanes apart, so the gain depends on the reply's adjacency terms. The screen is what shows it.
